source.title: Non-Vacuous Generalisation Bounds for Shallow Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper sweeps hidden-layer width and reports test error for naturally labeled MNIST and Fashion-MNIST networks, using erf and GELU activations rather than the version's ReLU networks and datasets.
record.gate_note: The study also reports non-vacuous generalization bounds and test errors in Table 1, but those are selected settings without a width comparison, so they do not establish the width claim. Random-label fitting and magnitude-aware sharpness are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study reports held-out error across hidden-layer widths, bearing on V2 with different activations and a fixed-loss stopping rule. It does not establish interpolation or resolve whether test error keeps decreasing beyond it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the width discussion but omits the main conclusion: the authors obtain non-vacuous bounds directly for deterministic shallow networks trained by SGD. They cannot resolve the true-error trend across widths, regard approximate width independence as plausible, and suspect worsening SHEL bounds with width is a bound artifact. GELU bounds better match that hypothesized width independence. Code and results are supplied in supplementary material.
record.recipe_differences: Width sweeps use single-hidden-layer erf or GELU networks, with SGD, on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST; the version describes ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, and zero training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test-error comparisons vary by activation, dataset, optimizer setup, learning rate, and width; error bars across seeds are shown for Figure 1.

fits_no_version.finding: The study obtains non-vacuous PAC-Bayesian bounds for deterministic shallow erf and GELU networks; bound behavior differs between the two activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization bounds for deterministic shallow networks can be non-vacuous using coupled data-dependent priors and majority-vote constructions.

record.problems: The text says the 10000-example test sets make width-related test-error differences below about 0.02 difficult to distinguish. Training targets fixed cross-entropy values rather than explicitly reporting zero training error. Many width-sweep values are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports selected test errors for SHEL and GELU networks on four datasets with and without momentum, but does not give width for each selected setting or compare test error across widths. Other figure sweeps compare learning rates rather than widths.

untested.parts: No reported results establish near-perfect random-label fitting together with natural-label generalization and chance random-label held-out accuracy. Section 5 mentions random relabelling but supplies no corresponding results.

Zero training error, the interpolation threshold, training to convergence, and continued improvement specifically beyond that threshold are not established. ReLU networks and downsampled CIFAR-10 are not evaluated in these sweeps.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No matched batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets; remarks about training stability do not establish held-out performance penalties.
No comparison of classifiers trained with and without dropout.
No magnitude-scaled sharpness ranking of generalization gaps within a convolutional family or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence and comparison with random removal.

missing.what: Additional width sweeps at momentum-SGD learning rates 0.1 and 0.001 for both activations and datasets. These are width comparisons, contrary to the record's statement that the other sweeps compare learning rates. Their curves cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: No directional verdict is justified: unresolved test-error trends do not demonstrate absence, reversal, or a scope limitation of V2. The authors' approximately 0.02 resolution argument is uncertainty, and their width-independence interpretation is explicitly conditional. Having more parameters than training examples does not establish zero training error.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.

The study does not establish that each width has zero training error or locate the width needed to interpolate; it uses erf and GELU activations, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, and does not test downsampled CIFAR-10.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Batch sizes differ across training setups, but the study does not report a matched comparison of test performance by batch size.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.

relation.reason: The study reports its own width-versus-test-error experiments, although their results cannot determine V2's effect.

tranche.reason: Width sweeps measure held-out error using different activations and fixed cross-entropy stopping criteria, bearing on V2 without establishing interpolation or a decreasing post-interpolation trend.

source_check.notes: Training stops at cross-entropy 0.1 on MNIST and 0.3 on Fashion-MNIST; momentum is 0.9 with batch size 200. Zero training error and interpolation width are not established; approximate width independence is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated reversal of V2.
